'''Isaiah Hartenstein''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|h|ɑr|t|ən|ʃ|t|aɪ|n}} {{respell|HAR|tən|shtyne}},<ref>{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=May 18, 2024}}</ref> {{IPA|de|ˈhaʁtn̩ʃtaɪn|lang|De-Hartenstein.ogg}}) (born May 5, 1998) is an American and German professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Listed at {{cvt|7|ft|0|in}}, Hartenstein plays the [[center (basketball)|center]] position.

Before playing in the NBA, Hartenstein played in Germany before playing in Lithuania for [[BC Žalgiris|Zalgiris Kaunas]], with which he won a [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|Lithuanian League]] championship in 2017. After he left Lithuania in 2017, the [[Houston Rockets]] selected him with the 43rd overall pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]], but he did not make his NBA debut with the Rockets until the next season. In 2024, Hartenstein signed with the Thunder and won the [[2025 NBA Finals]] in his first season with the team. He has also played for the [[Denver Nuggets]], [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]], [[New York Knicks]], and the [[Germany men's national basketball team|Germany national team]].

==Early life==
Born in [[Eugene, Oregon]], Isaiah Hartenstein is the son of {{interlanguage link|Florian Hartenstein|de}}, a basketball coach and former professional basketball player, and Theresa Hartenstein. His mother is a White American, and his father is half African-American and half German.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/sports/2017/06/isaiah_hartenstein_nba_draft_r.html|title=Isaiah Hartenstein goes from Eugene to the NBA after being drafted by Houston Rockets|last=Brown|first=Tim|date=June 23, 2017|website=oregonlive.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://people.com/isaiah-hartenstein-parents-everything-to-know-11985622|title=Meet Isaiah Hartenstein's Parents, Mom Theresa and Dad Florian Hartenstein|website=People|date=May 28, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.complex.com/sports/a/joshua-espinoza/isaiah-hartenstein-confirms-hes-part-black-im-bright-skin|title=Isaiah Hartenstein Discusses Being Part Black|first=Joshua|last=Espinoza|date=March 28, 2024|website=Complex}}</ref> Isaiah's parents met in the United States while his father played basketball at the [[University of Oregon]].<ref name="Zeit">{{cite web| last1 = Bieg | first1 = Peter | url = http://www.zeit.de/sport/2015-06/isaiah-hartenstein-basketball-talent | work = Die Zeit | title = Großer Mann, was nun?  | date = June 15, 2015 | access-date = February 2, 2016}}</ref>

In 2008, Hartenstein and his family moved to [[Germany]],<ref name="Artland">{{cite web| url = http://www.artland-dragons.de/fileadmin/site/pdf/Drachen-Bote/Drachen-Bote_15-03_April.pdf | work = Artland Dragons | title = Isaiah Hartenstein: "Mein Ziel ist die beste Liga der Welt"  | date = March 3, 2013 | access-date = February 2, 2016}}</ref> where his father was playing professionally.

==Professional career==
===Artland Dragons (2015–2016)===
Hartenstein joined the [[MTV Gießen]] youth ranks and continued his career at the youth teams of [[QTSV Quakenbrück]]/[[Artland Dragons]], after his father had signed to play with the [[Artland Dragons]] in 2009.

In the 2013–14 season, Hartenstein led the Artland Dragons' junior team to a German championship in the under-16 Bundesliga JBBL, while being named Most Valuable Player.<ref name="JBBL">{{cite web | url = http://www.nbbl-basketball.de/events/awards-jbbl/ | work = NBBL | title = Awards der Jugend Basketball Bundesliga | date = February 2, 2016 | access-date = February 2, 2016 | archive-date = April 14, 2015 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150414021312/http://www.nbbl-basketball.de/events/awards-jbbl/ | url-status = dead }}</ref> He averaged 20.9 points, 12.1 rebounds, 3.4 assists, 2.9 steals and 1.9 blocks on the season.<ref name="Stats">{{cite web | url = http://www.nbbl-basketball.de/teams/jbbl/nordwest/#rcd1:/statistik/spieler/index.php%3Fteam_id=2006&saison=2013&spieler_id=21532 | work = NBBL | title = Isaiah Hartenstein Steckbrief | date = February 2, 2016 | access-date = February 2, 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160914004145/http://www.nbbl-basketball.de/teams/jbbl/nordwest/#rcd1:/statistik/spieler/index.php%3Fteam_id=2006&saison=2013&spieler_id=21532 | archive-date = September 14, 2016 | url-status = dead }}</ref> His father Florian, who served as head coach of the team, was named JBBL Coach of the Year.

Hartenstein was selected to play in the 2014 [[Jordan Brand Classic]] International game. He finished the game with four points and five rebounds in 18 minutes.<ref name="JBC">{{cite web | url = http://jordanbrandclassic.com/wp-content/uploads/archive/2014internationalgameboxscore.pdf | work = Jordan Brand Classic | title = Official Basketball Box Score International Black vs International White | date = April 18, 2014 | access-date = February 2, 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160221163847/http://jordanbrandclassic.com/wp-content/uploads/archive/2014internationalgameboxscore.pdf | archive-date = February 21, 2016 | url-status = dead }}</ref>

On February 1, 2015, the 16 year old Hartenstein made his debut in Germany's [[German basketball league system|top-tier level]] [[Basketball Bundesliga]], seeing less than two minutes of action against [[Eisbären Bremerhaven]].<ref name="BBL">{{cite web | url = http://www.beko-bbl.de/de/n/spielberichte/2014-15/nachbericht/2015-02-01-bre-art/#specialnavi=33 | work = Basketball-Bundesliga | title = Boxscore Eisbären Bremerhaven – Artland Dragons | date = February 1, 2015 | access-date = February 2, 2016 | archive-date = April 10, 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160410074128/http://www.beko-bbl.de/de/n/spielberichte/2014-15/nachbericht/2015-02-01-bre-art/#specialnavi=33 | url-status = usurped }}</ref>

In August 2015, Hartenstein signed a deal with Lithuanian powerhouse [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]], but he remained with the [[Artland Dragons]] on [[loan (sports)|loan]].<ref name="Zalgiris">{{cite web| url = http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/69yd5rpubbe3mwhv/zalgiris-invests-in-top-german-talent-hartenstein | work = Euroleague | title = Zalgiris invests in top German talent Hartenstein  | date = August 17, 2015 | access-date = February 2, 2016}}</ref> The Dragons had withdrawn from the Bundesliga, and were [[promotion and relegation|relegated]] to the [[ProB|2. Bundesliga ProB]], Germany's third division. Hartenstein played in 14 games for [[Quakenbrück]] during the 2015–16 campaign, compiling averages of 11.6 points, 8.9 rebounds, 2.1 blocks, 1.6 steals and 1.4 assists.<ref name="2. Basketball-Bundesliga">{{cite web| url = http://www.zweite-basketball-bundesliga.de/teams/kader/spieler/2594/ | work = 2. Basketball-Bundesliga | title = Isaiah Hartenstein  | date = February 2, 2016 | access-date = February 2, 2016}}</ref>

===Žalgiris Kaunas (2016–2017)===
In January 2016, Hartenstein decided to leave the Artland Dragons to join Žalgiris Kaunas.<ref name="Quakenbrueck">{{cite web| url = http://www.eurobasket.com/Germany/news/435389/NBA-prospect-Isaiah-Hartenstein-leaves-Quakenbrueck | work = Eurobasket.com | title = NBA prospect Isaiah Hartenstein leaves Quakenbrueck  | date = January 22, 2016 | access-date = February 2, 2016}}</ref>

Hartenstein helped the Žalgiris Kaunas under-18 squad to win the qualifying tournament to the [[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] and was selected MVP.<ref name="ANGT">{{cite web| url = http://www.adidasngt.com/u18/game-center/games/showgame?gamecode=14&seasoncode=JTK15#!report | work = adidasngt.com | title = 2015–16 ANGT Kaunas Final  | date = January 17, 2016 | access-date = February 2, 2016}}</ref>

Hartenstein made his debut for Žalgiris in Lithuania's top-flight league, the [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|LKL]], on September 28, 2016, against Šiauliai<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.lkl.lt/zaidejas/2382875/|title=Isaiah Hartenstein {{!}} Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|website=Tete-a-Tete Casino-LKL|access-date=October 9, 2016|archive-date=October 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161009131438/http://www.lkl.lt/zaidejas/2382875/|url-status=dead}}</ref> and in the [[EuroLeague]] against [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahce]] on October 26.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=23&seasoncode=E2016#!boxscore|title=Fenerbahce Istanbul vs. Zalgiris Kaunas – Game|website=www.euroleague.net|access-date=October 31, 2016}}</ref> Later in that season, he helped Žalgiris win the first ever [[Karaliaus Mindaugo taurė|King Mindaugas Cup]].

===Houston Rockets / Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2017–2020)===
In February 2016, Hartenstein attended the "Basketball Without Borders Global Camp" during the [[NBA All-Star Weekend]] in [[Toronto]], Canada.<ref>{{Cite web| url = http://www.draftexpress.com/article/Basketball-Without-Borders-Global-Camp-Evaluations-Power-Forwards-5370/| title = DraftExpress: Basketball Without Borders Global Camp Evaluations: Power Forwards| website = www.draftexpress.com| access-date = February 28, 2016}}</ref> On April 7, 2017, he scored 10 points and grabbed three rebounds in 19 minutes of play at the [[Nike Hoop Summit]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.usab.com/news-events/live-stats/2017/usa-vs-world-select-team-2017.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170420123751/http://www.usab.com/news-events/live-stats/2017/usa-vs-world-select-team-2017.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 20, 2017|title=LiveStats – USA vs World Select Team – Nike Hoop Summit|access-date=April 8, 2017|language=en-US}}</ref>

Hartenstein declared for the [[2017 NBA draft]] on April 22, 2017. He also earned an invite to the [[2017 NBA Draft|2017]] [[NBA Draft Combine]], but he ultimately declined participation for the event. On June 22, 2017, he was selected with the 43rd overall pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]] by the [[Houston Rockets]]<ref>{{cite news|title=Rockets Select Isaiah Hartenstein in 2017 NBA Draft|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-draft-release|access-date=June 23, 2017|work=NBA.com|date=June 22, 2017}}</ref> and subsequently competed for the team in the [[2017 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 3, 2017 |title=Rockets to Compete in NBA Summer League 2017 |url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-compete-nba-summer-league-2017-0/ |access-date=July 11, 2017 |work=NBA.com}}</ref>

In the 2017–18 campaign, Hartenstein appeared in 38 games of the [[NBA G League]], averaging 9.5 points and 6.6 rebounds a contest for the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://gleague.nba.com/player/isaiah-hartenstein/|title=Isaiah Hartenstein – NBA G League|work=NBA G League|access-date=June 22, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref>

On July 25, 2018, the [[Houston Rockets]] signed Hartenstein.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rockets Sign Isaiah Hartenstein |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-isaiah-hartenstein |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 26, 2018 |date=July 25, 2018}}</ref> After being sent down to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]], he was suspended one game without pay after leaving the bench during an altercation in a 132–109 loss to the [[Memphis Hustle]] on December 17, 2019.<ref>{{cite news |title=Four Rio Grande Valley Vipers Players Suspended |url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/four-rio-grande-valley-vipers-players-suspended/|work=NBA.com|date=December 19, 2019|access-date=December 24, 2019}}</ref>

On February 7, 2019, Hartenstein recorded his first career triple-double after posting 12 points, 16 rebounds and 11 assists in a 103–102 road win against Salt Lake City Stars.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/game/2021800435/|title=Rio Grande Valley Vipers 103 – Salt Lake City Stars 102|publisher=G-League Stats|date=February 7, 2019|access-date=April 4, 2020}}</ref> In the 2018–19 season, Hartenstein scored 33 points and made a career-high 8 3-pointers in the series-clinching game as they won the [[NBA G League]] championship with the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/game/2041800402/|title=Long Island Nets 116 – Rio Grande Valley Vipers 127|publisher=G-League Stats|date=April 9, 2019|access-date=April 5, 2020}}</ref> He won the [[NBA G League Finals Most Valuable Player Award|NBA G League Finals MVP]] award.

On June 23, 2020, the [[Houston Rockets]] announced that they had waived Hartenstein.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-free-agent-david-nwaba-0|title=Rockets Sign Free Agent David Nwaba|date=June 23, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=June 23, 2020}}</ref>

===Denver Nuggets (2020–2021)===
On November 30, 2020, the [[Denver Nuggets]] announced that they had signed Hartenstein to a multi–year contract.<ref>{{cite news |title=Nuggets sign center/forward Isaiah Hartenstein |url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-isaiah-hartenstein-202011# |access-date=November 30, 2020 |work=NBA.com |date=November 30, 2020}}</ref> Playing behind the All-Star center [[Nikola Jokić]], Hartenstein averaged 9 minutes, 3.5 points and 2.8 rebounds per game.

===Cleveland Cavaliers (2021)===
On March 25, 2021, Hartenstein and two future second-round picks were traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in exchange for center [[JaVale McGee]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/hartenstein-trade-210326|title=Cavaliers Acquire Isaiah Hartenstein and Two Second Round Draft Picks from the Denver Nuggets|work=NBA.com|date=March 25, 2021}}</ref> In his first twelve games with the Cavs, Hartenstein averaged 19 minutes of playing time and 9 points, 7 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.4 blocks per game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Isaiah Hartenstein Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/harteis01.html |access-date=2025-06-24 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Clippers (2021–2022)===
On September 27, 2021, Hartenstein signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=LA Clippers|number=1442522813173092365|title=Ready to put in work.|user=LAClippers|date=September 27, 2021|access-date=October 2, 2021}}</ref>

===New York Knicks (2022–2024)===
[[File:Isaiah Hartenstein 2023 New York Knicks.jpg|upright|thumb|Hartenstein with the New York Knicks in 2023]]
On July 12, 2022, Hartenstein signed a two-year, $16 million contract with the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Knicks Sign Isaiah Hartenstein |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/knicks-sign-isaiah-hartenstein |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 12, 2022 |date=July 12, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams  |author-link=Shams Charania |date=June 30, 2022 |title=Isaiah Hartenstein, Knicks agree to 2-year, $16 million deal: Sources |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3489406/2022/07/01/isaiah-hartenstein-knicks-agree-to-2-year-16-million-deal-sources/ |access-date=July 16, 2022 |website=The Athletic}}</ref>

===Oklahoma City Thunder (2024–present)===
====2024–25 season====
On July 6, 2024, Hartenstein signed a three-year, $87 million contract with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Isaiah Hartenstein to Multi-Year Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-hartenstein-240706|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2024|access-date=July 6, 2024}}</ref> On November 20, he made his Thunder debut, putting up 13 points, 14 rebounds, five blocks, and three assists in a 109–99 win over the [[2024–25 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/thunder-news-shai-gilgeous-alexander-honest-take-isaiah-hartenstein-debut|title=Shai Gilgeous-Alexander honest take on Isaiah Hartenstein's Thunder debut|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pavon|first=Josue|date=November 21, 2024|access-date=November 21, 2024}}</ref> Hartenstein made 57 appearances (53 starts) for the Thunder during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 11.2 points, 10.7 rebounds, and 3.8 assists. In his first season with the Thunder, Hartenstein won his first NBA championship as the team defeated the [[2024–25 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana Pacers]] 103–91 in Game 7 of the [[2025 NBA Finals]]. He contributed seven points and nine rebounds in the clinching game.<ref>{{cite web | last=Young | first=Ryan | title=NBA Finals: Isaiah Hartenstein's son hilariously sleeps through trophy celebration after Thunder's win | website=Yahoo! Sports | date=2025-06-23 | url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/article/nba-finals-isaiah-hartensteins-son-hilariously-sleeps-through-trophy-celebration-after-thunders-win-035625276.html | access-date=2025-12-10}}</ref>

====2025–26 season====
On November 7, 2025, Hartenstein recorded a career-high 33 points, as well as 19 rebounds and three blocks in a 132–101 victory over the [[2025–26 Sacramento Kings season|Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Thunder's Isaiah Hartenstein: Logs career-high 33 points|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/thunders-isaiah-hartenstein-logs-career-high-33-points/|access-date=January 16, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}}</ref>

==== 2026–27 season ====
On June 26, 2026, Hartenstein re-signed with the Thunder on a three-year, $75 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Thunder to keep Hartenstein on new 3-year deal, sources say|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49193260/thunder-keep-hartenstein-new-3-year-deal-sources-say|access-date=June 30, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en|date=June 26, 2026|last=Charania|first=Shams}}</ref>

==National team career==
[[File:20171127 FIBA WCQ 2019 AUT-GER Isaiah Hartenstein 850 7283.jpg|thumb|upright|Hartenstein with the German national team in 2017]]
Hartenstein represented [[Germany men's national basketball team|Germany]] at the [[2014 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]]<ref name="U16">{{cite web| url = http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_YUjW-7-FJ,kK9s431Lyr41.roundID_9771.season_2014.teamID_288.playerID_108390.html | work = FIBA Europe | title = Isaiah Hartenstein, Germany  | date = January 17, 2016 | access-date = February 2, 2016}}</ref> and the [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]].<ref name="U18">{{cite web | url = http://u18men.fibaeurope.com/en/compID_8aYeHlfuGF-mF5IqO8aFH1.season_2015.roundID_11484.teamID_288.playerID_108390.html | work = FIBA Europe | title = U18 European Championship Men, Isaiah Hartenstein, Germany | date = February 2, 2016 | access-date = February 2, 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160202060408/http://u18men.fibaeurope.com/en/compID_8aYeHlfuGF-mF5IqO8aFH1.season_2015.roundID_11484.teamID_288.playerID_108390.html | archive-date = February 2, 2016 | url-status = dead }}</ref> He helped carry Germany to a fourth-place finish at the [[2016 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]], averaging team-highs of 14.7 points, 9.5 rebounds, 1.7 blocks, and 1.7 steals a contest,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u18/2016/Germany|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160703021824/http://www.fiba.com/europe/u18/2016/Germany|url-status=live|archive-date=July 3, 2016|title=Germany at the FIBA U18 European Championship Division A 2016 - FIBA.com|website=FIBA.com|access-date=December 22, 2016}}</ref> which earned him a spot in the tournament's "All-Star Five".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u18/2016/news/france-crowned-champions-at-fiba-u18-european-championship|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171006074913/http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u18/2016/news/france-crowned-champions-at-fiba-u18-european-championship|url-status=live|archive-date=October 6, 2017|title=France crowned champions at FIBA U18 European Championship|website=FIBA.com|date=December 22, 2016 |access-date=December 22, 2016}}</ref>

In August 2017, he made his debut with the German men's national team<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.sportschau.de/weitere/basketball/nationalmannschaft/basketballer-verlieren-ersten-em-test-100.html|title=Deutsche Basketballer verlieren ersten EM-Test|last=sportschau.de|date=August 5, 2017|access-date=August 6, 2017|language=de}}</ref> and took part in [[EuroBasket 2017]], averaging 4.3 points and 2.5 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Isaiah HARTENSTEIN (GER)'s profile|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2017/Isaiah-Hartenstein|website=FIBA EuroBasket 2017}}</ref>
